result.title: Closing Plenary
result.description:
Join this closing plenary to reflect on the ideas, partnerships and actions emerging from the Annual Meeting of Global Future Leaders. 

How can current and next-generation leaders translate foresight, dialogue and experimentation into strategies that advance resilience and shared progress?

result.title: Betazone: Sensing the Invisible
result.description:
The world around us is filled with signals we cannot hear, see or feel, from wireless activity in a room to biological signals beneath our skin and information moving through the ocean. New forms of sensing are beginning to make this hidden world visible.

What becomes possible when we can sense the world in entirely new ways?

Join engineer and scientist Fadel Adib for a visual journey into the emerging world of wireless sensing, exploring how new technologies can change how we understand and interact with the world, and the applications of these technologies across health, climate, retail, commerce, robotics, and more.
 
Speakers: Fadel Adib

result.title: Reading the Youth Pulse
result.description:
We keep asking young people what they want. The sharper question is what they already understand that the rest of us have yet to grasp. Drawing on the World Economic Forum’s Youth Pulse report, which captures the perspectives of nearly 10,000 young people across regions, this discussion explores the signals emerging from a generation growing up amid rapid change. 

What might today’s leaders need to unlearn to keep pace with the generation already adapting to what comes next?
 
Speakers: AbdelQader AlSaqqaf, Tiffany Lee, Kacha (Shogun) Mahadumrongkul, Khalid Mohammed Al Nuaimi, Sakshi Sharma

result.title: These economists won the Nobel prize for transforming policy-making
result.description:
The work of this year’s winners of the Nobel Prize for Economics has made central banks and governments ‘better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy’, says the committee chair.

New Nobel laureates Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford showed how economies are shaped by the decisions taken by individual households and businesses - and how those decisions, in turn, are shaped by people’s expectations of the future. Their work has helped transform how governments and central banks understand macroeconomic factors such as #inflation and unemployment, and has enabled policy-makers to respond far more effectively when crises appear.

Three times a year, the World Economic Forum canvasses chief economists from the public and private sectors on the state of the global #economy - and asks them to predict what lies in store. Read the most recent Chief Economists’ Outlook here: https://www.weforum.org/publications/chief-economists-outlook-september-2026

result.title: Economics after Certainty
result.description:
Economic policy-making has long relied on models that promise predictability. Yet repeated shocks, from inflation and financial crises to geopolitical fragmentation, have exposed the limits of forecasts and equilibrium thinking. 

As uncertainty becomes a defining condition, what would a more adaptive approach to economics look like, one that helps economies anticipate change, unlock new sources of growth and strengthen resilience?


 
Speakers: Abeer Abu Omar, Hamed Ali, Chinwe Egwim, Sergei Guriev, Ma Song, Milojko Spajić
